text:
alex: Quick async check — wrapping up the sprint item on continuous-batching + KV prefetch. Milestone: unblock canary by EOD Wed. Owners: kernel=cheng, kv=wren, infra=maya. Known blockers: warmup race on cold shards, seq-len mispredictions, and flaky CI. Any other blockers? TL;DR please.

cheng: On kernel fixes — found a race in the microbatch allocator when KV returns a zero-length prefix. Minimal repro in local tests. PR #812 opened with allocator fix and extra asserts. Need an eviction signal from KV to avoid reacquiring evicted segments. CC @wren.

wren: KV side here — eviction signal endpoint is implemented as an opt-in stream: {"evict_hint": true} (proto patch incoming). I'll open INF-459 with the proto and a small harness to replay many tiny prefixes. Question: do we want immediate evict notifications or batched hints?

maya: Infra can run a constrained canary with the eviction_stream enabled for one GPU pool. Ops will throttle traffic to 40% and limit sequences to 512. @ops-bot can you schedule the canary window?

ops-bot: deploy request acknowledged for canary: canary-cont-batch-evict -> scheduled at 2024-06-12T18:00Z, window 1h. Rollback triggers: 5xx > 0.5% OR p90 latency > baseline + 30ms. Monitoring watchers: eng-runtime on-call.

alex: Sounds good. Cheng/Wren — agree on the hint schema and a safe backstop? Also need a short blurb for Support about changed cache priming semantics.

olivia: I'll draft the support note now. Quick perf update: local perf run with batch size 8 shows throughput +18% but cold-start p95 +22ms.

cheng: Expected tradeoff. Adding async KV prefetch into the warmup path recovers ~15ms of that cold p95 in our bench. PR 812 includes an opt-in flag: --prefetch-warmup.

wren: One dependency to call out — quantization branch QNT-120 changes some key hashing order. If QNT lands before compatibility work, KV will see different keys and miss cache hits. KV team needs to provide a stable hashing compatibility layer or we gate QNT during the canary.

alex: Good catch. Action items and ownership: cheng -> land PR 812 by tomorrow noon; wren -> open INF-459 today with proto and harness; olivia -> publish support note by EOD; maya -> start canary at 18:00. Sam, can you also eyeball PR 812 metrics naming?

sam: Yep, left two comments on PR 812 re metrics naming (kernel.batch.size vs runtime.batch_size) — small rename will keep dashboards consistent.

cheng: addressing comments, will push an update in ~30m.

maya: Scheduling confirmed. I'll post canary link + Grafana panels in this thread before 18:00 and tag on-call.

alex: Perfect. If anything blocks the canary (esp. the QNT compat risk), call it out here immediately and we gate. @here escalate if we see regressions during the window. :thumbsup:
